{{Short description|80th edition of the Vuelta a España}} {{hatnote|For the women's race, see [[2026 La Vuelta Femenina]].}} {{Infobox cycling race report | name = 2026 Vuelta a España | series = [[2026 UCI World Tour]] | race_no = 31 | season_no = 36 | image = La Vuelta (Spain) logo.svg | image_size = | image_caption = | image_alt = | date = 22 August – 13 September | stages = 21 | distance = 3310.6 | unit = km | time = 73h 52' 55" | first = [[Enric Mas]] | first_nat = ESP | first_team = {{UCI team code|MOV men|2026}} | first_color = red | second = [[Primož Roglič]] | second_nat = SLO | second_team = {{UCI team code|RBH|2026}} | third = [[Felix Gall]] | third_nat = AUT | third_team = {{UCI team code|DCT|2026}} | points = [[Wout van Aert]] | points_nat = BEL | points_team = {{UCI team code|TVL men|2026}} | points_color = dark green | mountains = [[Santiago Buitrago]] | mountains_nat = COL | mountains_team = {{UCI team code|TBV|2026}} | mountains_color = blue polkadot | youth = [[Oscar Onley]] | youth_nat = GBR | youth_team = {{UCI team code|NCI|2026b}} | youth_color = white | combativity = [[Wout van Aert]] | combativity_nat = BEL | combativity_team = {{UCI team code|TVL men|2026}} | combativity_color = yellow number | team_nat = FRA | team = {{UCI team code|DCT|2026}} | team_color = red number | previous = [[2025 Vuelta a España|2025]] | next = ''[[2027 Vuelta a España|2027]]'' }} The '''2026 Vuelta a España''' was a three-week cycling race taking place in [[Monaco]], [[France]], [[Andorra]] and [[Spain]]. It started on 22 August in [[Monaco]] and finished on 13 September in [[Granada]].{{cite web|title=Official route of La Vuelta 2026|url=https://www.lavuelta.es/en/overall-route|website=lavuelta.es|date=17 December 2025|access-date=23 December 2025}} It is the 81st edition of the [[Vuelta a España]] and the third and final [[Grand Tour (cycling)|grand tour]] of the [[2026 in men's road cycling|2026 men's road cycling season]]. The [[general classification in the Vuelta a España|general classification]] was won by [[Enric Mas]] of {{UCI team code|MOV|2026}}. Although [[Tadej Pogačar]] ({{UCI team code|UEX|2026}}} was widely expected to win the GC, and won three of the first six stages, he was injured in a crash on the eighth stage and forced to withdraw from the race. Mas, who was in second place when Pogačar crashed, inherited the red jersey, won the ninth stage, and defended his lead until the end of the Vuelta. The [[points classification in the Vuelta a España|points classification]] was won by [[Wout van Aert]] ({{UCI team code|TVL|2026}}}, who also won two stages and the overall [[combativity award]]. Van Aert's teammate [[Matthew Brennan (cyclist)|Matthew Brennan]] won five stages, more than any other competitor. [[Santiago Buitrago]] ({{UCI team code|TBV|2026}}) won the [[mountains classification in the Vuelta a España|mountains classification]], and [[Oscar Onley]] ({{UCI team code|NCI|2026b}}), placing sixth in the overall GC standings, won the [[young rider classification in the Vuelta a España|young rider classification]]. == Teams == {{Main|List of teams and cyclists in the 2026 Vuelta a España}} Twenty-three teams took part in the race. All eighteen [[UCI WorldTeam|UCI WorldTeams]] were automatically invited. They were joined by five [[UCI ProSeries|UCI ProTeams]]; the three highest ranked UCI ProTeams in 2025 ({{UCI team code|TUD|2026}}, {{UCI team code|PQT|2026}} and {{UCI team code|COF men|2026}}), along with two other Spanish teams ({{UCI team code|BBH|2026}} and {{UCI team code|EKP|2026}}). The teams were announced on 30 January 2026.{{Cite web |title=LA VUELTA 26: TEAM SELECTION - La Vuelta 2026 |url=https://www.lavuelta.es/en/news/2026/la-vuelta-26-team-selection/51093 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.lavuelta.es |language=en}} === UCI WorldTeams === {{div col|colwidth=20em|style=margin-right:20%;}} * {{UCI team code|APT|2026}} * {{UCI team code|DCT|2026}} * {{UCI team code|EFE|2026}} * {{UCI team code|GFC|2026}} * {{UCI team code|LTK men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|LOI|2026}} * {{UCI team code|MOV men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|NCI|2026b}} * {{UCI team code|NSN|2026}} * {{UCI team code|RBH|2026}} * {{UCI team code|SOQ|2026}} * {{UCI team code|TBV|2026}} * {{UCI team code|JAY men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|TPP men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|UEX|2026}} * {{UCI team code|UXM men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|TVL men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|XAT|2026}} {{div col end}} === UCI ProTeams === {{div col|colwidth=20em|style=margin-right:20%;}} * {{UCI team code|BBH|2026}} * {{UCI team code|COF men|2026}} * {{UCI team code|EKP|2026}} * {{UCI team code|PQT|2026}} * {{UCI team code|TUD|2026}} {{div col end}} == Pre-race favourites == Five-time Tour de France champion [[Tadej Pogačar]] (UAE Team Emirates) arrived to the Vuelta regarded as the presumptive winner of the race, but retired from the race after crashing during the eighth stage. The Slovenian held a big lead in the race but got caught in a crash near the end of the stage. He tried to rejoin the race but was unable to due to severe injuries to his clavicle and spine, and was taken by ambulance to hospital. Race organizers confirmed he pulled out of the race.[https://www.cyclingnews.com/pro-cycling/teams-riders/tadej-pogacar-abandons-the-vuelta-a-espana-after-crash-on-stage-8/ Cycling News report on Pogačar] Other contenders for the general classification include [[Felix Gall]] and [[Richard Carapaz]], as well as 4-time winner [[Primož Roglič]], despite having been hit by a car during training just 3 weeks before the start.https://www.cyclingstage.com/vuelta-2026-vuelta-2026-favourites/contenders-spain-2026/ In the competition for the green jersey, [[Mads Pedersen]] and [[Wout van Aert]] were considered the favourites.{{Cite web |date=2026-08-22 |title=Five contenders for the points classification at the 2026 Vuelta a España |url=https://www.domestiquecycling.com/en/news/five-contenders-for-the-points-classification-at-the-2026-vuelta-a-espana/ |access-date=2026-08-30 |website=Domestique Cycling |language=en}} == Route and stages == The official route was announced on 17 December 2025 in [[Monaco]].{{Cite web|last=Fotheringham|first=Alasdair|date=18 December 2025|title=Vuelta a España 2026 route|url=https://www.cyclingnews.com/pro-cycling/races/vuelta-a-espana-2026-route/|access-date=23 December 2025|website=Cyclingnews|language=en}} {| class="wikitable" |+ Stage characteristics and winners |- !
